chapter: Image, travel and Black, Brown and Beige
title: Hollywood Bowl and closing with Mood Indigo
summary: Greer describes closing programs with Diminuendo and Crescendo, then Mood Indigo with pinpoint lights.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: You know, in California. I know one time we played Hollywood Bowl. You know, that's a big place, too. We played "Black, Brown and Beige,"
we closed down -- we shook them up. We played that near the end and after we played that we went to something sweet, you know. Either "Sophisticated Lady" or --
"I Let A Song Go Out of My Heart" (Inaudible) or one of those pretty tunes.
Yeah, but we closed the program with "Mood Indigo" or something like that. And we played this "Diminuendo" and "Crescendo". You've got a record of that?

We laid that on them to stir them up, you know. And Molly, bar the door, that was it. Yeah. But all our theater programs, we always closed it with "Mood Indigo." Stage blacked out, just big, pinpoint lights on trombones, clarinets, and Carnev, baritone. And I was singing way in the distance, high falsetto, obbligato.
Oh, right, you mentioned that. You mentioned that you also put that on them when you were in Europe in that white --
That's right. That's how we closed our act.
Yeah, you told me you put it on them in Europe.
And they'd never seen that. They would dim down, at the end of it, complete blackout. And man, you could hear a pin drop (inaudible). Lights went up, man, that was it.
